We are committed to building a diverse, global team and our sponsorship policy is evaluated on a role-by-role basis. We encourage you to keep an eye on our careers site to stay informed about future opportunities where we are able to offer visa sponsorship.</em></p> <p>Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today's challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future. Leveraging Data, AI, and real-time decision-making we turn energy complexity into growth opportunities for our partners.&nbsp;</p> <p>By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable and affordable.</p> <p>With teams across Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen</p> <p><strong>What will I be doing?</strong></p> <p>Reporting to the VP Product &amp; Tech Operations, you’ll own the timely, predictable execution of our Product &amp; Technology roadmap, for Kaluza and for our clients, across our global product, field deployment, and platform foundations teams. You’ll line-manage Heads and Group Delivery Managers, set the standard for how delivery is done across the function, and provide the leadership confidence around what we can deliver, both near-term and further ahead. You’ll move fluently between board-level narrative and the detail of a single stuck dependency.</p> <p><strong>The role spans four focus areas:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Run delivery at scale </strong>- own predictable, end-to-end execution across your portfolio.</li> <li><strong>Implementing an AI-native system of wor</strong>k - make AI-assisted delivery the default and raise the bar on how delivery is done, partnering with our P&amp;T business operations team to implement best practices across our product development lifecycle (PDLC) that are designed and standardised by the Business Operations team.</li> <li><strong>Grow an independent, high-performing delivery community</strong> - build a function that solves its own problems, and has a “yes if” attitude to solving the inevitable challenges of the day to day.</li> <li><strong>Partner and Influence at the Executive Level&nbsp;</strong></li> </ul> <h1><span style="font-size: 18pt;"><strong>Run delivery at scale</strong></span></h1> <p>Own and drive successful delivery across Kaluza’s Product and Tech organisation, typically multiple streams that may align to client programmes or global initiatives.</p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end delivery of the Product &amp; Tech roadmap across your area, e.g. across multiple client streams (OVO &amp; ENGIE in Europe, AGL &amp; Shell in APAC) or multiple global product streams.</li> <li>Implement evolutions of a standard methodology that allows the business to scale and ensures successful client implementations</li> <li>Drive absolute roadmap alignment, delivery enablement and reporting at multiple levels, from team detail to executive overview.</li> <li>Bring confidence to what we can deliver, near-term and further ahead through robust capacity planning, milestone tracking (actuals vs estimates), forecasting, and proactive management and resolution of cross-team dependencies.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Engineering, UX and Client Delivery leadership so deliverables meet client capabilities, support needs and timelines, and so client feedback flows back into the delivery process.</li> <li>Provide objective, data-led neutral insight on how delivery is really going; proactively escalate risks and issues early, and drive decisions with senior leadership and clients.</li> <li>Embed good practices into our internal delivery management practices that are developed by the Business Operations team, and provide input to shape their future roadmap.&nbsp;</li> <li>Deputise for the VP when needed.</li> </ul> <h1><span style="font-size: 18pt;"><strong>Implement an AI-native system of work through delivery</strong></span></h1> <p>Lead the strategic evolution of our delivery practices by embedding AI-assisted methodologies into default operational workflows</p> <ul> <li>Embed AI-assisted delivery into reporting, forecasting, capacity and effort analysis, dependency mapping, risk detection and status communication.</li> <li>Push the boundaries of Jira, JQL and agentic workflows; build dashboards and reporting that drive development forward at pace and replace manual effort.</li> <li>Simplify and standardise practice across Product &amp; Tech: refine ways of working, embed Agile &amp; Lean practice, and raise predictability and the effort-to-value ratio in your area.</li> <li>Act as a change driver, co-own the delivery of a roadmap of improvements to our system of work alongside Business Operations, and bring people with you through the change.</li> <li>Champion continuous improvement and show the function what good, AI-native delivery looks like in practice.</li> </ul> <h1><span style="font-size: 18pt;"><strong>Grow an independent, high-performing delivery community</strong></span></h1> <p>Build a self-sufficient, empowered function that is a gold standard for getting things done, effectively, and with transparency.</p> <ul> <li>Lead and develop a group of people leaders and delivery managers, Heads of, Group and Lead) Delivery Managers, setting clear objectives, focus and clarity.</li> <li>Coach the team to navigate complexity and uncertainty, to self-solve, and to bias their effort towards Kaluza’s goals and our client commitments.</li> <li>Know the product and coach the team to understand the product domain for their area so that they can enable cross-functional team delivery of the product roadmap and client delivery goals</li> <li>Mentor and upskill across the community; show the team what good looks like and raise the standard across the board.</li> <li>Clear the barriers that stop Product teams focusing on innovation and strategy, and Engineering teams focusing on technical excellence and execution.</li> <li>Support the Delivery function in achieving its strategy and goals, and champion the wider change and planning agenda.</li> <li>Be an innovative thinker and member of the larger Kaluza SLT team to drive the business forward.</li> </ul> <h1><span style="font-size: 18pt;"><strong>Partner and Influence at the Executive Level&nbsp;</strong></span></h1> <ul> <li>Act as a trusted partner to Product, Engineering, UX, and Client Delivery leadership, serving as an active member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT)&nbsp;</li> <li>Confidently manage relationships with C-level clients.&nbsp;</li> <li>Deliver objective tracking, milestone visibility + forecasting, and proactive risk mitigation strategies to leadership, while serving as a strategic deputy for the VP of Product &amp; Tech Operations when required</li> </ul> <p><strong>About You</strong></p> <p>You’re an accomplished delivery leader with a strong track record. Ideally, you’ll be:</p> <ul> <li>A builder <em>and</em> an executor: you define what good looks like, take full accountability, and go looking for what you need rather than waiting for a brief.</li> <li>Genuinely AI-native: AI tools feel like leverage, not an afterthought. You have deep curiosity in innovation and AI tools, actively pushing AI adoption into delivery practice.</li> <li>Steady in ambiguity: A nimble leader who thrives in complex undefined spaces, is comfortable diving into problems at multiple altitudes, and the steady presence others rely on when the path isn’t fully defined.</li> <li>Strategic Delivery Leader: An accomplished delivery leader and a bar raiser when it comes to of managing large-scale, cross-functional delivery management functions within a high-growth SaaS environment</li> <li>Experienced leading delivery management at scale: line-managing and developing people leaders, across cross-functional Product &amp; Engineering teams using agile methodologies.</li> <li>Able to design and evolve delivery operating models, governance and ways of working, with an openness to follow current Kaluza practice and refine where needed.</li> <li>A trusted partner: to Product &amp; Engineering leadership, able to influence senior leadership,and credible with C-level clients.</li> <li>A strong listener, people leader <em>and</em> coach: able to empower teams and colleagues to reach their full potential, and to bring people along on a change journey.</li> <li>Fluent with Jira, or similar roadmapping tools, with real curiosity about using JQL and AI to generate dashboards and reporting that drive development at pace.</li> <li>Comfortable switching between team-level detail and executive-level overview, applying the right approach in the right context.</li> <li>Committed to radical candour: you ask hard questions, and give honest developmental feedback.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What will set you apart</strong></p> <ul> <li>Extensive experience managing delivery frameworks across major global energy utility accounts or multi-regional client programmes.</li> <li>A proven background or curiosity in implementing an AI-integrated Product Development Lifecycle alongside business operations teams.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Where you'll work</strong></p> <p>We offer flexible working, with a requirement of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.</p> <p><strong>Kaluza Values</strong></p> <p>Here at Kaluza we have five core values that guide us as a business:</p> <p><strong><em>Play to win, Solve the real problem, Build trust every day, Own the outcome, Go further together.</em></strong></p> <p><strong>Our Perks</strong></p> <ul> <li>Pension Scheme</li> <li>Discretionary Bonus Scheme</li> <li>Private Medical Insurance + Virtual GP</li> <li>Life Assurance</li> <li>Access to Furthr - a Climate Action app</li> <li>Free Mortgage Advice and Eye Tests</li> <li>Perks at Work - access to thousands of retail discounts</li> <li>5% Flex Fund - to spend on the benefits you want most</li> <li>26 days holiday + bank holidays</li> <li>Progressive Leave Policy - With no qualifying service periods, including up to 26 weeks full pay for primary caregivers and 4 weeks full pay for secondary caregivers when welcoming a new addition to your family.</li> <li>Personal Learning Budget - Upskill, learn and grow!</li> <li>Home Office Budget</li> <li>And more!</li> </ul> <p><strong>We want the best people</strong></p> <p>We’re keen to meet people from all walks of life. Our view is that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We want to build teams which represent a variety of experiences, perspectives and skills, and we recognise talent on the basis of merit and potential.</p> <p>We understand some people may not apply for jobs unless they tick every box. But if you're excited about joining us and think you have some of what we're looking for, even if you're not 100% sure, we'd still love to hear from you.</p> <p>Find out more about working in <a href="http://kaluza.com">Kaluza</a> on our <a href="https://kaluza-dev.webflow.io/careers">careers page</a> and <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/kaluza/">LinkedIn</a>. <br><br>You can also find our Applicant Data Protection Policy <a href="https://www.kaluza.com/applicant-data-protection-notice">here</a>.</p> <p><br><br><br></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

For us, recruitment is a team sport - we win together, constantly looking at how we can improve and bounce ideas off each other, and always step in to help whenever someone gets stuck or hits a wall.</p> <p>Our<strong> Consumer Mission </strong>- building the <a href="https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sumup.pay&amp;hl=en">SumUp App</a> - is scaling fast and we’re looking for a Senior Tech TA Partner to help the team navigate London’s hyper-competitive market, where top engineers are in high demand.Your superpower will be understanding how to position SumUp's massive scale and impact to passive talent. title: Senior Product Data Analyst- Consumer Growth
description: <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.</p> <p>As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.</p> <p>We’re looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You’ll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.</p> <p>You’ll help answer questions such as:</p> <ul> <li>Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?</li> <li>Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?</li> <li>What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?</li> <li>Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?</li> <li>How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?</li> </ul> <p>If you’re motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from <strong>acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation</strong>.</li> <li>Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.</li> <li>Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.</li> <li>Support decisions that improve key business description: About Us   IVC Evidensia is the UK and Europe’s leading veterinary care group, made up of over 900 practices and referral hospitals, united by a shared purpose of happier animals, happier owners.  At IVC Evidensia, we believe careers should be built without limits. Our people are supported to make more impact, access more career opportunities, and play an active role in their local and professional communities. Through investment in learning, innovation, and wellbeing, we create environments where our teams can grow in confidence, capability, and fulfilment—at every stage of their career.  As part of Central Functions, you will be part of the teams that support and enable our network of over 2,500 practices across 20 countries, driving operational excellence, innovation, and strategic impact across the business.   Our Technology teams are responsible for the systems and infrastructure that make that work - everything our healthcare professionals need to deliver world-class care. From keeping on top of patient records, health plans, client communications, diary management and dispensing, our teams have a lot to think about and need smarter ways to provide the convenience and expertise that modern Pet owners have come to expect. IVC Evidensia is undergoing an exciting digital transformation. The key to this is improving the management of our core data sets - accelerating the standardisation of operational systems in practices, building stronger master data management tooling, and developing standard reporting models across the group. As a data engineer, you will work with the team to advance the data platform within a DevOps culture. You will play a central role in building and maintaining scalable data pipelines across Databricks & Azure SQL Server, and will bring solid experience with ELT, orchestration, and scripting languages. A firm grasp of data modelling and management will be essential throughout. The role The Data Engineer will be a technical authority accountable for the design and development of the technologies that underpin our data strategy. At the heart of this is our Databricks data platform, and you will take ownership of building, optimising, and maintaining data pipelines using PySpark - orchestrating feeds from source systems through to our group data platform and taking technical ownership of all parts of the process. You will work closely with the business to deliver solutions that address real challenges, engaging with SMEs to break requirements into deliverables. You will also collaborate with the Data Architect to shape our overarching data management strategy. What you'll bring to the role We're looking for a technically skilled and business aware individual with a strong understanding of data concepts, including storage, processing, and modelling. Core requirements include: Databricks - hands-on experience building and managing workloads on the Databricks platform, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and Declarative Automation Bundles PySpark - proficiency in writing and optimising PySpark code for data transformation and processing Azure - solid experience working within the Azure ecosystem, including services such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake Storage, and Azure DevOps Azure SQL Server - experience with Azure SQL Server is important, as it forms the foundation of our existing data warehouse. You will be working across both our SQL Server environment and our Databricks platform, and an understanding of how the two integrate will be key to success in this role ELT & pipeline development - experience designing and maintaining pipelines using REST APIs, JSON, and ELT protocols Data modelling - comfort working with both relational and non-relational data technologies, with a solid grounding in modelling principles Exposure to business intelligence tools like Power BI is desirable. You'll act as a key interface between IT and functions such as Finance and Marketing, so excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills are vital. You should be confident working within an Agile framework, with an understanding of secure development practices and non-functional requirements such as scalability, performance, and access management. An international mindset, sensitivity to local business priorities, and a collaborative approach are essential. What’s in it for you?   At IVC Evidensia, we’re committed to supporting your development and wellbeing. When you join us, you’ll benefit from:  A role with real business impact supporting teams across the organisation  Clear career pathways with progression opportunities within Central Functions and beyond  Ongoing learning and development supported by tailored programmes and resources  A collaborative, values-led culture focused on care, innovation, and continuous improvement  Flexible working with a remote first working policy Benefits   Healthcare Cash Plan  Cycle to Work scheme  Green Cars salary sacrifice scheme  Voluntary benefits: choose from a range of benefits to suit you  Discounted staff pet care   Access to discounts/cashback with hundreds of participating retailers    Diversity, Equality, Inclusion and Belonging   At IVC Evidensia we are committed to Diversity, Equality, Inclusion and Belonging, we are keen to hear from candidates from all minority and diverse groups. raw.description:
About Sine Engineering

Sine Engineering builds the technology behind reliable drone autonomy, including communications, navigation, and control systems that enable coordinated multi-drone operations at scale.

More than 200 UAV manufacturers rely on our technologies, and our solutions power many of today's active interceptor operations. Through our dual-use platform, we support civilian innovation while helping democratic nations strengthen their technological advantage.

Any Drone. Any Scale. Anywhere. We build resilient communication, navigation, and coordination systems for the age of autonomy.

We are looking for a Sales Director to lead and scale our commercial organization in a fast‑growing defence technology company building cutting‑edge solutions for the drone era. This is a high‑impact leadership role responsible for shaping sales strategy, driving revenue growth, and building a world‑class sales team in a complex, mission‑critical environment.

You will operate at the intersection of advanced technology and global markets, working with sophisticated customers and stakeholders across defence, aerospace, and related industries. The role requires a strong mix of strategic thinking, operational discipline, and hands‑on deal leadership, particularly in long sales cycles and multi‑stakeholder environments.

 

As Sales Director, you will define and execute go‑to‑market strategy, improve commercial performance, and ensure sales excellence across forecasting, pipeline management, and deal execution. You will also play a key role in scaling the organization, developing talent, and shaping how we engage with strategic customers and partners globally.

 

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and manage a team of Account Executives and Key Account Executives

  • Set targets, sales cadence, and pipeline management standards

  • Drive forecasting discipline, deal reviews, and performance management

  • Build and improve sales processes, coverage models, and territory/account allocation

  • Support major negotiations and strategic deals

  • Align sales execution with product, operations, finance, legal, and leadership

  • Recruit, onboard, and develop sales talent

  • Ensure CRM data and sales reporting are accurate and decision‑useful

  • Identify gaps in commercial performance and implement improvements

  • Contribute to pricing strategy, sales planning, and go‑to‑market execution

  • English: C1 preferred; strong B2 acceptable if other qualifications are strong

 

Experience

  • Strong B2B sales leadership experience in a complex or technical environment

  • Proven ability to build, manage, and improve a team‑based sales organization

  • Strong forecasting, pipeline management, and commercial decision‑making skills

  • Experience with complex deals, long sales cycles, and multi‑stakeholder selling

  • Strong coaching and performance management capabilities

  • Excellent executive communication and cross‑functional influence

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience in defence, aerospace, electronics, telecom, or industrial manufacturing

  • Experience building sales processes in a scaling company

  • Familiarity with channel models, strategic OEM sales, or international expansion

If this role resonates with your experience and ambitions, we invite you to apply and take the next step in shaping high‑impact customer partnerships in a rapidly evolving defence technology landscape.

 

Location: Europe (Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, UK)

 

Culture Statement

Don’t meet every requirement? Research shows that many candidates hesitate to apply unless they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Sine Engineering, we value authenticity and encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t perfectly match every requirement.

You may be the ideal candidate for this role - or for another opportunity with us.

Join our team and help shape the future of UAV technology.

By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data for recruitment purposes. Your data will be handled in accordance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

description: <p><strong><span data-contrast="none">Our roster has an opening with your name on it</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559739&quot;:160,&quot;335559740&quot;:276}">&nbsp;</span></strong></p> <p>We're looking for a Product Manager to join our Payments team, a domain that touches every customer who plays on FanDuel. You'll work closely with engineering and design to bring initiatives from scoping through delivery, while also contributing to the bigger questions of what we build and why — assessing opportunities, shaping priorities, and using data to inform decisions.</p> <p>The Product Manager ensures successful product performance through market analysis, a deep understanding of customer needs, and objective data analysis and reporting. Initiatives will be a mix of back-end and front-end work, with a focus on data driven recommendations, cutting edge technology and ease of use. There is a great opportunity to work across a range of expert teams to achieve your outcomes.</p> <p>In addition to the specific responsibilities outlined above, employees may be required to perform other such duties as assigned by the Company. This ensures operational flexibility and allows the Company to meet evolving business needs.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong><span class="TextRun MacChromeBold SCXW37208457 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW37208457 BCX0">The Role</span></span></strong><span class="LineBreakBlob BlobObject DragDrop SCXW37208457 BCX0"><strong><span class="SCXW37208457 BCX0">&nbsp;</span></strong></span></span></p> <ul> <li>Partner with engineering and design to drive execution of product initiatives — from scoping and requirements through launch and iteration</li> <li>Contribute to product discovery and prioritization, helping assess opportunities and shape the roadmap alongside your team</li> <li>Build and maintain relationships across engineering, design, data, operations, and other stakeholders to drive alignment and remove blockers</li> <li>Track product performance and use data to identify what's working, what isn't, and what to do about it</li> <li>Develop expertise in the payments domain and stay curious about how our product, customers, and competitive landscape evolve</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What We’re Looking For</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree preferred</li> <li>1+ years in a product management or product-adjacent role; prior PM title not required</li> <li>Excellent numerical and analytical skills with the ability to interpret data quickly to inform the right decisions</li> <li>Experience working with engineering and/or design teams, even in a supporting capacity</li> <li>Naturally resourceful — you ask questions, seek out the right people, and find a path forward even when the answer isn't obvious</li> <li>Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to make sense of data and present your thinking clearly across different audiences</li> <li>Comfortable managing competing priorities and working through ambiguity</li> <li>Don’t check all the boxes? That’s okay! We encourage you to still apply if you feel like you possess an adjacent skill set and are interested in learning more about this position</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What You Can Expect</strong></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Interesting work</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;"> - working in a fast-paced and ever-changing industry, new problems and exciting solutions are never too far away. There are always opportunities to learn new skills and broaden your horizons</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>A sense of achievement</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;"> - Our teams own their own software and when that awesome new feature ships to users and the positive feedback starts rolling in, you can feel really proud of what you and your team created</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Personal development</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;"> - clear and defined career pathways for every role at every level, a supportive manager, loads of learning opportunities and even 10% of your time to dedicate to your learning.</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Belonging</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;"> - everyone at FanDuel works for each other, we win together, make mistakes together and have lots of fun doing it.</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Trust - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">A trusting work environment where productivity is valued above all else, giving you autonomy and ownership of your time and work</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Great financial package </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">- Including salary, bonus, pension, private healthcare, share save scheme, flexible working &amp; holiday policy along with a number of other benefits.</span></li> </ul> <p style="text-align: center;">&nbsp;</p> <p style="text-align: center;">&nbsp;</p> <p style="text-align: center;"><strong>ABOUT FANDUEL</strong></p> <p>FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product. &nbsp;</p> <p>In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.</p> <p>The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.</p> <p>FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT).</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Diversity, Equity and Inclusion</strong></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">FanDuel is an equal opportunities employer. Diversity and inclusion in FanDuel means that we respect and value everyone as individuals. We don't tolerate bias, judgement or harassment. Our focus is on developing employees so that they reach their full potential.</span></em></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">FanDuel is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><em>At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit <a class="_ymio1r31 _ypr0glyw _zcxs1o36 _mizu194a _1ah3dkaa _ra3xnqa1 _128mdkaa _1cvmnqa1 _4davt94y _4bfu18uv _1hms8stv _ajmmnqa1 _vchhusvi _kqswh2mm _ect4ttxp _syaz13af _1a3b18uv _4fpr8stv _5goinqa1 _f8pj13af _9oik18uv _1bnxglyw _jf4cnqa1 _30l313af _1nrm18uv _c2waglyw _1iohnqa1 _9h8h12zz _10531ra0 _1ien1ra0 _n0fx1ra0 _1vhv17z1" href="http://klaviyo.com/careers" data-renderer-mark="true">klaviyo.com/careers</a>&nbsp;to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny.</em></p></div><p><strong>London, UK (Hybrid: 3 days p/week in-office)<br></strong><strong>FTC (ASAP to May 2027)&nbsp;<br></strong></p> <p><strong>About the role:<br>This is a fixed term contract for an ASAP start until May 2027. We are looking for an experienced hands-on Senior Localisation Program Manager to own and optimise&nbsp;<span style="text-decoration: underline;">Product localisation.</span></strong></p> <p>Localisation efforts at Klaviyo are centred around linguistic excellence, teamwork and scale. We are responsible for the translation and cultural adaptation of all customer-facing content from performance-based marketing collateral to original training programs, the Klaviyo application and website, and our partner and developer portals. Our work is not just about translation and localization; it is about providing our customers with high quality localization and an experience that feels locally relevant and fuels international growth for both our customers and Klaviyo. Your primary responsibilities will be to:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Manage all localisation for Product, Help Centre and Customer Education</strong>, partnering closely with those teams to deliver high quality, locally relevant experiences across all supported languages.</li> <li><strong>Manage all language contractors</strong> (including freelance linguists, agencies and other language vendors), ensuring we have the right resourcing, quality, cost and workflows in place to support current and future localisation needs.</li> <li><strong>Contribute to scaling localisation overall</strong>, including the management of machine translation for all languages and helping to build an AI-first translation platform that enables faster, more scalable and more cost-effective localisation for Klaviyo.</li> </ol> <p><strong>How You’ll have an impact:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>End-to-end localisation ownership for Product, Help Centre and Customer Education</strong>: Plan, execute and manage localisation solutions for the Klaviyo Product, Help Centre and Customer Education teams, partnering closely with those teams to fully understand business goals, priorities and opportunities.</li> <li><strong>Contractor and vendor management</strong>: Source, onboard, train, develop and manage a highly effective network of linguists and language partners (including freelancers, agencies and other vendors) that consistently deliver high-quality output across all languages and content types.</li> <li><strong>Language quality management</strong>: Define clear expectations and quality standards for all languages, set up scalable review and feedback loops, and manage performance to ensure we meet or exceed quality, timeliness and cost targets. Own and manage the Klaviyo Language hub (language governance) and associated processes across all languages.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>TMS and MT ownership</strong>: Own and manage our TMS (Smartling) as it relates to Product, Help Centre and Customer Education, ensuring optimisation for different content types, CMSs, language assets and resources, and integrating and managing machine translation within our workflows for all supported languages.</li> <li><strong>AI-first translation platform</strong>: Partner with Engineering, Product, Data and other internal teams to help design and build an AI-first translation platform that leverages MT, generative AI and automation to increase localisation speed, consistency and scalability while maintaining quality.</li> <li>Transform workflows by putting AI at the centre, building smarter systems and ways of working from the ground up.</li> <li><strong>Collaboration across the Localisation team</strong>: Collaborate with the broader Localisation team to deliver a high-quality localised experience for international customers, drive scale in localisation, and resolve issues and blockers quickly.</li> <li><strong>Champion the international customer</strong>: Be a champion internally for the international Klaviyo customer, ensuring their needs are represented in content, product decisions and localisation priorities.</li> <li>Perform other related duties as assigned.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who you are:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in a comparable localisation role on the buyer/ client side</li> <li>Deep understanding of localisation concepts, methodologies, tools and assets, and demonstrated experience of designing and implementing localisation solutions at scale, including hands-on experience with TMS and MT/ AI-driven workflows</li> <li>Experience leading product localisation across multiple languages</li> <li>Ability to to partner with internal teams and influence roadmaps to title: Staff Analytics Engineer
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. Please note: applications are open until 2nd September 2026 09.00 CEST. We will not review any application before the closing date. Please do not rush and use this time to submit a high quality application! About the role This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in. The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it. For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot. Who you'll work with You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary. What you'll be doing Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational. Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity. Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick. Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it. Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform. Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention. Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream. Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow. What you bring Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage. Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains. Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust. AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase. A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority. Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime. Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business. Why this role is a good fit for you This role is a good fit if: You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy. You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards. You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with. This role is not a good fit if You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to. You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have. You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use. Your first 6 months By the end of your first six months, you'll have: Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into. Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc. Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated. Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why. The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment. Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application: We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background. Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. Prior experience owning a semantic layer is also a non-negotiable. Make sure your application reflects this. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here . Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role. Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

Please note: applications are open until 2nd September 2026 09.00 CEST. We will not review any application before the closing date. Please do not rush and use this time to submit a high quality application!

About the role

This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in.

The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it.

For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot.

Who you'll work with

You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational.

  • Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity.

  • Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick.

  • Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it.

  • Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform.

  • Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention.

  • Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream.

  • Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow.

What you bring

  • Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage.

  • Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains.

  • Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust.

  • AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase.

  • A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority.

  • Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime.

  • Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business.

Why this role is a good fit for you

This role is a good fit if:

  • You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy.

  • You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards.

  • You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with.

This role is not a good fit if

  • You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to.

  • You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have.

  • You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use.

Your first 6 months

By the end of your first six months, you'll have:

  • Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into.

  • Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc.

  • Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated.

  • Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why.

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals.

  3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team.

  4. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise.

  5. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

  • We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.

  • Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. Prior experience owning a semantic layer is also a non-negotiable. Make sure your application reflects this.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

raw.title: Staff Analytics Engineer
raw.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

Please note: applications are open until 2nd September 2026 09.00 CEST. We will not review any application before the closing date. Please do not rush and use this time to submit a high quality application!

About the role

This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in.

The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it.

For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot.

Who you'll work with

You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational.

  • Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity.

  • Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick.

  • Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it.

  • Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform.

  • Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention.

  • Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream.

  • Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow.

What you bring

  • Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage.

  • Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains.

  • Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust.

  • AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase.

  • A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority.

  • Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime.

  • Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business.

Why this role is a good fit for you

This role is a good fit if:

  • You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy.

  • You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards.

  • You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with.

This role is not a good fit if

  • You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to.

  • You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have.

  • You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use.

Your first 6 months

By the end of your first six months, you'll have:

  • Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into.

  • Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc.

  • Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated.

  • Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why.

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals.

  3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team.

  4. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise.

  5. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

  • We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.

  • Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. Prior experience owning a semantic layer is also a non-negotiable. Make sure your application reflects this.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.
